name: TX-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Pat Fallon with a large financial advantage ($1.1M cash vs. $2K)
Challenger Jason Pearce raised only ~$16K with no outside support
Prediction markets price Fallon at ~95% to win
model.rationale: Fallon holds every advantage: a heavily Republican seat, incumbency, and a roughly 60-to-1 cash edge over Pearce, who has raised almost nothing. Markets price the race at about 95% Republican, consistent with the fundamentals, so the forecast stays near the baseline with a slightly wider Republican margin.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending for Pearce or a major scandal involving Fallon would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-04 is a solidly Republican northeastern Texas district, and incumbent Pat Fallon is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. His challenger, Democrat Jason Pearce, has run a minimal campaign, raising about $16,000 with roughly $2,000 on hand, while Fallon has raised nearly $800,000 and holds more than $1 million in cash. No outside groups are spending against Fallon, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Fallon about a 95% chance of winning, and the district's partisan lean points to a comfortable double-digit Republican margin. Absent unexpected developments, Fallon is positioned to win decisively in November.
